Let me analyze the teaching examples more carefully to identify the systematic errors and correction rules.

Looking at Example 1 (2025-01-10):
- Model forecasts are consistently LOWER than true outcomes for days 1-25
- At day 30, model is slightly higher (76.88 vs 74.02)

Looking at Example 2 (2025-01-09):
- Same pattern: model lower than true for days 1-25
- At day 30: model 77.53 vs true 74.02 (over by 3.51)

Looking at Example 3 (2025-01-08):
- Days 1-4: model lower (71.22 vs 72.17, 71.69 vs 73.46, 72.43 vs 74.85, 73.58 vs 76.92)
- Days 5-9: model slightly higher but not enough (73.13 vs 76.96, etc.)
- Days 10-25: model lower again
- Days 26-30: model higher by ~1-2 points

Looking at Example 4 (2025-01-07):
- Days 1-3: model lower
- Days 4-9: model slightly higher (but true is higher so this might just be less than expected)
- Days 10-25: model lower
- Days 26-30: model higher

Looking at Example 5 (2024-05-10):
- Days 1-4: model lower (71.02 vs 71.59, 69.09 vs 70.07, 68.64 vs 70.10, 67.37 vs 69.19)
- Days 5-9: model slightly higher but not enough
- Days 10-25: model lower
- Days 26-30: model higher

So the pattern seems to be:
1. Model consistently underforecasts for days 1-25 (the "catch-up" happens at day 30)


2. Model overforecasts by 2-3 points for days 26-30

I notice a clear reversal pattern in the forecasts. The model shifts from underestimating prices to slightly overestimating them in the final quarter of the 30-day horizon. This consistent divergence suggests a potential systematic bias in the original forecasting model, particularly in the early and late periods of the prediction window.
